open_issues: Nothing in the product starts the queue (the review's missing spec item, unchanged and deliberately left alone). IOcrQueue.ResumeAsync/DrainAsync still have no caller outside tests: starting the resume on session open and the drain on an idle pass is shell work and is outside this package's 'App.xaml.cs DI lines only' allowance. It needs assigning explicitly to B3-2b. Note for whoever gets it: OcrQueue is Scoped over the session's WakeelDb, which in the desktop is one context shared with the Blazor UI, so the drain must run in its own scope or EF will throw its second-operation error.
No scanner is attached to this machine, so WiaScanner's COM paths — including the FindDevice release fix — are still unexercised by any test and were verified by reading only.
notes:
COMMAND RUN EXACTLY AS GIVEN, ALL GREEN. src/Wakeel.Core, src/Wakeel.Ocr, src/Wakeel.Desktop, tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests --no-dependencies: 0 warnings, 0 errors each. dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests --no-build: 682 passed, 1 skipped (the pre-existing Word skip), 683 total. tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests: 340 passed. tests/Wakeel.Walkthrough.Tests: 24 passed (it was 20 at review time; another package added four concurrently, all green). Totals above are the three suites added together. Seven new tests, all in tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests/Documents. Nothing outside the allowed paths was touched, no package was added, no git state command was run.

PER FINDING.

1 (medium, cancelled part-read filed as read). OcrQueue.ReadCoreAsync now keeps the partial pages AND puts the document back in line: after SavePagesAsync it calls SetOcrStatusAsync(OcrStatus.Pending) when result.State == OcrState.Cancelled. Two things beyond the suggested fix were needed. First, both writes go through CancellationToken.None, because the token that stopped the reading is already cancelled — the suggested `SavePagesAsync(..., cancellationToken)` followed by a cancelled SetOcrStatusAsync would have thrown out of DrainAsync instead of recording where the reading stopped, and my first test run proved exactly that. Second, the zero-pages branch had the same latent problem, so its SetOcrStatusAsync picks None for the cancelled case too. New test A_document_stopped_halfway_keeps_its_pages_and_stays_in_line: FakeEngine gained StopAfterPage/StopSource, reports page 1..3 of 20, cancels the real token at page 3 and returns OcrState.Cancelled with those three pages (what OcrService does). It asserts OcrStatus.Pending plus three saved pages, then that a fresh OcrQueue's ResumeAsync finds it (returns 1, Pending contains it) and a drain finishes it to Done with PageCount 20 and twenty page rows.

2 (medium, audit actor "system"). DocumentService gained `private string? _actor;` and ActorAsync, mirroring CorrespondenceService line for line (AsNoTracking over Installation, EmployeeName, cached per scope because a scope is one session). StoreAsync passes it instead of the literal. Test The_audit_line_names_the_person_who_added_the_file asserts the document.added row's Actor equals world.Installation.EmployeeName. A grep now finds no literal actor anywhere in src/Wakeel.Core.

3 (medium, IsAvailable false negative on ScanAsync). The guard is now `_scanner is null` alone, with a comment saying why: only "no scanner support in this host" is decided in Core, and whether the machine also has a device is the scanner's own answer, since asking it to scan is what looks. To test it rather than assert it by reading, FakeScanner now models the real cached probe instead of a settable flag: HasDevice says whether the machine really has one, `IsAvailable => _saw` starts false and is only set by ListDevicesAsync or a scan — the same shape as WiaScanner._sawScanner. Two tests: Scanning_before_the_device_list_was_ever_asked_for_still_scans asserts !scanner.IsAvailable and then a stored page, which fails on the old guard; A_machine_that_has_a_scanner_answers_the_words_only_when_it_really_has_none keeps the «لا ماسح ضوئي» sentence for HasDevice false. The existing Without_a_scanner_the_answer_is_words_and_not_a_failure (no scanner registered at all) is untouched and still passes.

4 (low, COM leak in FindDevice). The loop body is wrapped in try/finally with a `keep` local set immediately before each `return info;`; the finally releases when !keep. Both `continue` paths now release, as ListDevices already did. Read-verified only — no scanner on this machine.

5 (low, fingerprint blind to a same-size swap). Fingerprint hashes name:length:LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks per file, with the reason written into the XML doc. New test A_replacement_of_the_same_size_is_still_noticed writes a different 100-byte ara.traineddata, sets a later write time, and asserts the fingerprint changed — the existing test only changed the length and still passes.

6 (low, tools\tessdata reachable from an installed product). The walk-up candidate only yields <dir>\tools\tessdata when <dir>\Wakeel.slnx exists (new private const SolutionFileName). Verified the tests still find the repository copy: OcrServiceTests ran 10 tests with 0 skipped, and the real-pixel Arabic/English [OcrFact] passed, so Find() still resolves D:/AI/Administration2/tools/tessdata from the test bin folder five levels up.

7 (low, a PDF of zero pages). ScanPdfWriter.Combine counts the pages it actually wrote and throws the same ArgumentException as the empty-input case when the count is 0. Because that turns a previously-silent case into a throw on a path Core calls, DocumentService.ScanAsync was restructured to match: it binds first into a local `bound`, catches ArgumentException, and falls through to the existing "store the sheets separately" branch — so the office keeps its work either way and nothing unopenable is ever stored. Tests: Sheets_that_are_none_of_them_pictures_are_refused_rather_than_bound_into_nothing (two undecodable sheets through the real Skia writer) and Sheets_the_binder_cannot_make_a_document_of_are_kept_as_separate_pictures (a RefusingPdfWriter stub, asserting two PNG documents).

8 (low, counters outside the lock). _done increments in DrainAsync and ReadNowAsync moved inside lock (_gate); Report reads done and total as a pair under the same lock. _total was already incremented under the lock at both sites the finding named, so only the reads needed pairing with it.

9 (low, garbled XML doc). IDocumentService.ScanAsync's summary rewritten as suggested; it now points at ScanState.NoScanner, which is what the method actually answers, instead of DocumentImportState.KindNotAccepted.
